Definition: Does the government maintain a digital business register?
Comments: OBFC operates an Online Companies Registry System allowing the public to search the register and lodge documents for registration online; core company information migrated to the online system (evidence of digital business register).
revision_notes: Verified the OBFC Company Registry site (still live) confirming an Online Companies Registry System with free public search and online lodging of incorporation/maintenance documents; core company data was migrated from paper files. A 2025 LNDC knowledge-base page confirms manual lodgement remains available for clients without internet access, consistent with a partially (not fully) digitally deployed register. Score of 4 (Partially deployed) confirmed.
revised_comments: Lesotho's Registrar of Companies operates the Online Companies Registry System via the One-Stop Business Facilitation Centre (OBFC), enabling free public search of the register and online lodging of documents for incorporation and company maintenance. Core company records have been migrated to the online system, but clients without internet access can still lodge manual filings, indicating a digital register that operates alongside residual paper-based processes rather than an exclusively online system.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: Voter registration uses national ID as a primary document but also allows passport/affidavit alternatives, indicating linkage to national ID is present as a requirement/use case but not a fully integrated register-to-register system.
revision_notes: Verified IEC voting identification requirements (National ID/passport/driver's licence accepted). Fresher evidence (PublicEye News, Jan 2024) confirms the IEC and Ministry of Home Affairs are negotiating a shared database so a voter's record would auto-populate once their ID number is entered - described explicitly as a revived, not-yet-operational collaboration after an earlier attempt was abandoned when Home Affairs withdrew. This confirms integration remains at the planning stage rather than an operational technical link. Score of 2 (Planned) confirmed and re-dated to 2024 evidence.
revised_comments: Voter registration in Lesotho requires presentation of a National ID card (or passport/driver's licence as alternatives), and re-registration drives since 2024 have used the National ID card as the primary credential under the National Identity Card Act 2011. However, the Independent Electoral Commission and the Ministry of Home Affairs have not yet established an automated database link between the electoral register and the National Identity Register; a data-sharing collaboration to allow voter records to auto-populate from ID numbers was under renewed negotiation as of early 2024, after an earlier attempt had been abandoned.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital land register?
Comments: Lesotho Land Administration Authority provides an online Land Administration System/portal (LAOS) for land administration services, indicating a digital land registration platform is in place (availability appears limited to business hours, suggesting not fully mature nationwide always-on service).
revision_notes: Verified the LAA's Landfolio-based Land Administration Online System (LAOS), which gives registered users direct online access to view leases, plots, bonds and deeds, submit documents, and make payments. A 2025 LNDC knowledge-base summary confirms the LAA continues to manage land registration, cadastral survey and lease administration through this system. This supports a digital land register that is operational but confined largely to leasehold administration and available only during business hours - i.e. partially rather than fully deployed. Score of 4 (Partially deployed) confirmed.
revised_comments: The Lesotho Land Administration Authority (LAA) operates the Land Administration Online System (LAOS), built on the Landfolio platform, giving registered users direct online access to leases, plots, bonds and deeds and enabling online submission of documents and payments. The system underpins the LAA's core land registration, cadastral survey and lease administration functions, but focuses on leasehold titles rather than all land tenure types and is accessible only during business hours, indicating a digital register that is operational but not a fully deployed, always-on nationwide system.

Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: National Identity Register coverage reported as over 85% of eligible population (over 1.2m out of 1.4m eligible) and described as “close to universal coverage,” implying very high uptake relative to target population.
revision_notes: Multiple corroborating sources (World Bank blog 2021, World Bank GovTech case study 2022, Biometric Update 2021, CIPESA 2022) consistently report that Lesotho's National Identity Register covers approximately 85% of the eligible population (c.1.2m of 1.4m eligible). 85% falls within the 70-89% band on the metadata scale, corresponding to Value Code 4, not Value Code 5 (>89%). No source found supporting coverage above 89%. Original Value Code of 5 does not match the cited evidence; recalculated to 4.
revised_comments: Lesotho's National Identity Register, maintained by the Department of National ID and Civil Registry within the Ministry of Home Affairs, covers an estimated 85% of the eligible population, equivalent to around 1.2 million of a total eligible population of 1.4 million people. This is above the sub-Saharan Africa average of 71% but leaves an estimated 200,000 people, disproportionately those in remote rural areas, without a national ID.

Definition: Does the government maintain one or more tax registers?
Comments: Revenue Services Lesotho launched e-payment and e-taxation platforms enabling online tax payment and e-filing; RSL provides online taxpayer e-registration forms (individual and business), indicating a digitized tax register exists (not necessarily universal).
revision_notes: Verified the gov.ls announcement (2023) that Revenue Services Lesotho (RSL) launched e-payment and e-taxation platforms enabling online tax payment and e-filing of returns. eservices.rsl.org.ls confirms live online individual and business taxpayer e-registration forms. This is consistent with a digitised tax register that is operational but not confirmed as covering all taxpayers or as fully nationwide. Score of 4 (Partially deployed) confirmed.
revised_comments: Revenue Services Lesotho (RSL) operates e-payment and e-taxation platforms, launched in 2023, that allow taxpayers to file tax returns and pay taxes online, and maintains live online e-registration forms for both individual and business taxpayers. This constitutes an operational digital tax register, though coverage of the full taxpayer base and integration with all tax types is not confirmed as complete.

Definition: Does the register manage income tax, business taxes or both?
Comments: RSL e-taxation/e-services cover both individuals (income tax) and businesses, and TIN is used across Income Tax, Customs/Excise, and VAT, indicating coverage of both income and business taxation registration.
revision_notes: Verified RSL registration guidance confirming a single Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) is allocated for Income Tax, Customs & Excise, and VAT, and that both Individual Taxpayer and Business Taxpayer e-registration forms exist. This directly supports coverage of both income and business taxpayers under a linked TIN system. Value Code 4 (Both income and business taxpayers) is the maximum on this variable's scale; per protocol this confirmation is flagged for human review despite clear supporting evidence.
revised_comments: Lesotho's Revenue Services Lesotho (RSL) tax register covers both individual/income taxpayers and business taxpayers under a single Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), used consistently across Income Tax, Customs and Excise, and VAT. Separate online e-registration forms exist for individual and business taxpayers, both linked to the same TIN framework, indicating unified digital coverage of both taxpayer categories.
